title: Preparedness: Fragile
body: The Department has people, rooms, and procedures. It does not yet have margin. Every new demand is solved by borrowing attention from another problem.

title: Preparedness: Operational
body: Routine demands can be met without improvising every response. The distinction between routine and exceptional remains under active review.

title: Preparedness: Hardened
body: The Department can sustain pressure now. Some senior staff privately question whether this is resilience or simply a better-organized form of overwork.

title: Preparedness: Overextended
body: The Department can respond almost anywhere. It has begun to discover that capability attracts obligations faster than it creates relief.

title: Intelligence Quality: Anecdotal
body: The records contain names, claims, coordinates, and warnings. They do not yet agree on what any of them mean.

title: Intelligence Quality: Structured
body: Patterns are beginning to survive contact with additional evidence. Analysts have started pinning fewer questions to the walls and drawing more lines between them.

title: Intelligence Quality: Correlated
body: Independent sources reinforce one another. The most troubling connections are the ones that recur without being requested.

title: Intelligence Quality: Predictive
body: The Department sees movement before it understands it. This has improved response time and made some personnel uncomfortable with the implications.

title: Public Trust: Contested
body: The Department is visible enough to be blamed and obscure enough to be distrusted. Both conditions are operationally expensive.

title: Public Trust: Tolerated
body: Most people accept the Department when it remains useful, distant, and difficult to describe.

title: Public Trust: Established
body: The Department's authority is broadly accepted. The communications office reminds everyone that acceptance is not the same thing as understanding.

title: Public Trust: Resilient
body: Confidence survives difficult disclosures. The Department has earned room to explain itself, which may be more dangerous than having none.

title: Corruption Pressure: Contained
body: Controls are holding. The Oversight archive is quiet, though no one calls that reassuring.

title: Corruption Pressure: Latent
body: Small exceptions are accumulating. Each one has a justification. Together, they are beginning to resemble policy.

title: Corruption Pressure: Entrenched
body: Compromise is shaping decisions before those decisions are written down. The Department is still documenting the difference between adaptation and surrender.

title: Corruption Pressure: Critical
body: The Department may no longer be able to investigate itself without assistance from the systems it was created to monitor.

title: Staff Stress: Steady
body: Personnel are tired in ordinary ways. Recovery remains possible between cases.

title: Staff Stress: Strained
body: Recovery has become a scheduling problem. Staff are beginning to measure time off by what it fails to repair.

title: Staff Stress: Exhausted
body: The Department is functioning through accumulated fatigue. Errors are still individual; patterns are not.

title: Staff Stress: Breaking
body: Personnel systems are approaching failure. The reports remain professionally written, which is part of the problem.
